newsitem.title: FINLAND: Aamulehti sees good 97 operating earnings.
newsitem.headline: Aamulehti sees good 97 operating earnings.

text.p: Finnish media group Aamulehti Oy said on Thursday it expected operating earnings in 1997 to be good and overall group profit would show a clear improvement due to the sale of its Aldata unit.
"The consolidated result of operations is expected, as in 1996, to be good," Aamulehti said in a statement with its 1996 earnings.
"The gain on the Aldata divestment will make a clear improvement to the year's overall result."

"According to current forecasts the Finnish economy will enter a faster period of growth. This is expected to have a positive impact on both newspaper circulations and advertising revenues," Aamulehti said.
But it was difficult to forecast advertising revenue because Finland's first commercial radio and second commercial TV channel are due to start up this year, increasing competition.
Aamulehti made a gain of approximately 60 million markka on the sale of the Aldata information technology arm, which it said would be used to cover confirmed losses from earlier years. @
It said its Alpress newspaper unit would develop favourably with no major changes expected in newspaper circulations.
"Newspaper advertising revenues, however, should show a modest rise."
The reduced price of newsprint plus rationalisation measures completed during 1996 "are expected to improve the division's profitability on the previous year", it said.
"Alprint's profitability depends more on the external value of the Finnish markka and market developments in Russia than on demand in the domestic Finnish market. @
"Alprint's net sales are expected to remain at current levels unless changes in the value of the markka negatively affect western exports and rapid changes take place in the Russian markets.

"Exports to Russia are not expected to have such a decisive effect as during the previous year. The downward trend in paper prices will make a slight rise in operating volumes possible in the domestic market as well."
Overall net sales "are expected to reach the previous year's level with the existing corporate structure", Aamulehti said.
